chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn, from Fadala, from Hisham ibn al-Hudhayl, from Abu al-Hasan (the preceding Imam) peace be upon him, who said:
I asked him about the time of the Fajr prayer, so he said: 'When the dawn appears and you see it like a flowing river.'

key_terms.نَهَرِ سُورَاءَ: A flowing river (metaphor for the spread of dawn light)

ai.seo_question: What is the visual sign for the beginning of Fajr prayer time according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) provides a precise astronomical marker for the onset of Fajr prayer, distinguishing it from the earlier 'false dawn' (al-fajr al-kadhib) by describing the horizontal band of light resembling a flowing river. This definition is central to Shia fiqh for determining the exact start of the prayer window, ensuring the prayer is performed within its prescribed time before sunrise. The imagery of 'Nahar Surah' reflects the classical understanding of atmospheric light dispersion, emphasizing clarity in ritual timing.
